chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad (I think he is), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) or from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding the man who divorces his wife with one divorce, then divorces her a second time before he has had sexual intercourse with her, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The second divorce does not take effect until he has had intercourse with her.'

Then, other than that, are the previously mentioned reports, because it is permissible for us to specify these reports with the report we narrated in detail, for if we did not do that, we would nullify the ruling of the detailed report entirely and also nullify the ruling of the previously mentioned reports that included the permissibility of divorce without observing intercourse, and that is not permissible. And according to the manner we mentioned, we have reconciled all the hadiths.

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever divorces his wife while she is menstruating, after consummating the marriage with her, not being away from her, the divorce does not take effect. That is indicated by what he narrated.
ai.seo_question: Does the second divorce take effect if the husband divorces his wife twice without having intercourse after the first divorce?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between reports allowing immediate divorce and those requiring consummation by prioritizing the detailed narration, thereby establishing that a second divorce remains suspended until the couple resumes marital relations. This principle of reconciling specific and general reports ensures the validity of all transmitted traditions while clarifying that divorce during menstruation is valid but not immediately effective if the husband is present. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the physical consummation as a prerequisite for the finality of the first divorce in the three-divorce sequence.
